purpose: One composable form field that wraps **any** control — `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput`, `PasswordInput`, `PhoneInput`, `InputGroup`, `Combobox`, `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `Slider` — with its label, description and error. The root `Field` owns the field state (`invalid`, `disabled`, `required`) and the ids, and shares them through `provide`/`inject`: the control picks up its `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from the Field, `Field.Label` points its `for` at the control and shows the Required marker, and `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` register themselves so the control is described by them. Grouping parts (`Field.Set`, `Field.Legend`, `Field.Group`, `Field.Content`, `Field.Title`, `Field.Separator`) build fieldsets, choice cards and settings rows. One anatomy serves every control, so there is no per-control field wrapper.
useWhen: Use Field (Field.Label, Field.Description, Field.Error) around every form control; it wires the id, the required marker and the error for you. Field.Description and Field.Error also work alone, under a control that is not inside a Field; for a one-sentence explanation beside a label use Hint.
Any labelled form control: a text input, a select, a textarea, a password, a phone number, a slider.
A checkbox, radio or switch with its label beside it (`orientation="horizontal"`).

A selectable checkbox or switch card: `Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field` (replaces the v5 `*-block` variants). For one choice among cards use `RadioGroup variant="card"`, never a radio inside a `Field.Label`.
A group of related controls under one caption (`Field.Set` + `Field.Legend`), or a form section (`Field.Group`).
avoidWhen: A control with no visible label inside a toolbar or a table cell → render the control alone with an `aria-label`.
A group of mutually exclusive cards with icons → use `radio-group` with `type="card"`.
related: `input-group` — wraps an input with addons; put it inside a `Field` and use `InputGroup.Input` as the control.
`phone-input`, `password-requirements` — a phone number control and the live password rules row, each placed inside a `Field`.
bestPractices: Put the state on the `Field`, not on the control: `<Field invalid>` sets `aria-invalid` on the control and the invalid tone on `Field.Description`.
Let the Field own the ids. Pass an explicit `id` on the control and `for` on `Field.Label` only when another part of the page needs the id (focusing the first invalid field, an error summary link).

Render `Field.Description` for guidance and `Field.Error` for a validation message; both are announced through `aria-describedby`. `Field.Error` has `role="alert"`, so render it only when there is an error.
Choice cards: `<Field.Label><Field orientation="horizontal">control + Field.Content</Field></Field.Label>`. Never nest a choice card inside another `Field`; group cards with `Field.Set`.

Use `orientation="responsive"` for settings rows that stack in a narrow container and sit side by side in a wide one; it follows the nearest container (a `Field.Group`, a Card, a dialog or drawer body).
